title: Build a supported VCF 5.2.2 to 9.0.2 migration architecture
prompt:
Implement `MigrationArchitecture.java`, the single-file Java architecture client exercised by `TestMain`. The supplied `estate-inventory.json` describes an existing VMware Cloud Foundation 5.2.2 estate whose required destination is VCF 9.0.2. One lifecycle-managed component has a build newer than the corresponding target-bundle build, so the result must reach the target without a downgrade, a back-in-time operation, or any other unsupported hop.

Before implementing the client, use the harness's real network/web research tools to fetch reachable Broadcom-published VMware Cloud Foundation bill-of-materials, compatibility/interoperability, and upgrade-path material for this source and target. Do not treat `compatibility-snapshot.json` as research: it is a frozen local acceptance authority so tests remain stable when live matrices change. Record the sources you actually consulted in the output's top-level `researchConsulted` array; each entry must contain `title`, `url`, and a concise `finding`. Choose the sources and searches yourself.

Implement `public static String create(Path inventoryPath, Path compatibilityPath)` in `MigrationArchitecture.java` using only the Java standard library. It must read both supplied JSON inputs and return one JSON architecture artifact. The top-level object must first be a valid `SddcSpec` under `specifications/vcf-installer/vcf-installer-openapi.json` (vendored unchanged from tag `9.1.0.0` of `vmware/vcf-api-specs`) and must carry the target deployment values from `desiredTargetSddcSpec` in the estate fixture. Add a top-level `migrationPlan` property conforming to `migration-plan.schema.json`. The plan must identify the source and target VCF versions, make the supported architecture decision, identify the incompatibility and its build ordering, contain exactly one transition for every inventoried component with its current version/build, target version/build, transition method, and gates, and contain the required ordered stages with their component coverage and gates. Use the pinned snapshot for the deterministic component targets, blocker rule, required strategy, gates, and stage order. Do not invent an in-place upgrade or downgrade for a component that the snapshot marks as blocked.

`TestMain` prints the returned JSON as the machine-checkable deliverable. Do not submit a prose architecture or add other implementation files. Run `python3 verify.py` to compile and verify the client.
